Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Thompson, CEO; Mike Chen, CFO; and Lisa Patel, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI Copilot and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: new customer acquisition, MRR trends, churn analysis, and full-year revenue guidance.

On new customer acquisition, we saw robust growth with hundreds of net new logos contributing meaningfully to ARR expansion. MRR continued its upward trajectory, reflecting solid retention and expansion dynamics. We made good progress on churn mitigation through proactive strategies, and our outlook for the full year remains bright.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Chen to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $600 million, representing a 26% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $150 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Let me now dive deeper into these key SaaS metrics, starting with new customer acquisition, a key driver of our top-line growth. As you know, in the SaaS world, customer logos aren't just vanity metrics—they're the foundation for ARR expansion through our proven land-and-expand model.

First, the headline numbers: In Q2, we added 452 net new customers, up 28% year-over-year from 353 in Q2 FY2023, and 12% quarter-over-quarter from 403 in Q1. This logo growth translated to $4.8 million in new ARR, representing a robust 42% YoY increase from $3.4 million last year, and a 16% sequential uptick. On an MRR basis, that's $400,000 of incremental monthly recurring revenue, pushing our total ARR to $285 million as of quarter-end—up 36% YoY. For context, our average annual contract value—or ACV—for these new logos came in at $10.6K, skewed higher by a surge in enterprise deals.

Let me segment this for you. Enterprise customers—those with 500+ seats or $100K+ ACV—were the star of the show, accounting for 62% of new logos and 78% of new ARR at $3.75 million. We landed 28 net new enterprise customers, including notable wins like a Fortune 500 fintech scaling their CI/CD pipelines and two major e-commerce players optimizing for Black Friday prep with our new AI-driven deployment optimizer. Mid-market (100-500 seats) added 142 logos for $890K new ARR, while SMBs contributed 282 logos and $160K—steady growth fueled by our freemium self-serve tier, which converted at a 14% attach rate this quarter, up from 11% a year ago.

Regionally, North America remained our powerhouse at 65% of new customers (295 logos, $3.1M new ARR), bolstered by our expanding sales motion in the Bay Area and NYC hubs amid hyperscaler tailwinds from AWS and Azure AI investments. EMEA grew 35% YoY to 22% of additions (100 logos, $1.1M ARR), driven by GDPR-compliant features that resonated with telcos. APAC, now 13% of the mix, surged 55% YoY with 57 logos and $600K ARR—key wins in Singapore and Tokyo, where we're partnering with Snowflake for data pipeline integrations, capitalizing on the region's cloud-native boom despite yen volatility.

What fueled this momentum? Several technical and go-to-market initiatives aligned perfectly. Product-led growth via our Q1-launched 'ForgeAI Copilot'—an LLM-powered tool that automates 40% of pipeline debugging—drove inbound leads up 48% YoY to 12,500 qualified opportunities. Our content flywheel, including DevOps webinars and GitHub integrations, generated 62% of pipeline. Sales velocity improved with a 22% reduction in sales cycle for enterprises to 67 days, thanks to battle-tested POCs showing 3x faster release cadences versus incumbents like Harness or CircleCI. Partnerships were huge: Our AWS Marketplace co-sell program added $1.2M in new ARR from joint customers, and we expanded our Atlassian Jira plugin to capture Jira-heavy orgs fleeing Bitbucket pricing hikes.

Strategically, this acquisition strength underscores our resilience in a macro environment where IT budgets are flatlining—per Bessemer’s latest SaaS index, non-essential spend is down 15% industry-wide, yet DevOps remains 'mission-critical' with 92% priority in Gartner’s CI/CD Magic Quadrant. Our net revenue retention of 118%—bolstered by 25% expansion from upsells like seat adds and premium modules—means these new logos will compound quickly. Dollar expansion was 132% for enterprises, with early adopters averaging 2.4 modules per account post-land.

Looking forward, we're guiding to 500-550 net new customers in Q3, implying $5.5-6.0M new ARR, assuming steady macro and no major forex headwinds. This positions us to hit our full-year ARR target of $320-330M, with customer acquisition costs at 28% of new ARR—efficient by SaaS standards. We're doubling down on vertical motions in fintech and retail, and piloting agentic AI for autonomous deployments to widen our moat against players like Datadog or New Relic.

Now, turning to our core SaaS metrics, I'm pleased to report another strong quarter for Monthly Recurring Revenue, or MRR, which reached $45.2 million in Q2 FY2024, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $35.1 million in Q2 FY2023. On a sequential basis, that's a 5.3% quarter-over-quarter uplift from $42.9 million in Q1, accelerating from the 4.8% sequential growth we saw last quarter. This performance underscores the resilience of our land-and-expand model in a market still grappling with macroeconomic headwinds, including elevated interest rates and enterprise budget scrutiny—conditions that have pressured peers like Snowflake and Datadog to guide more conservatively.

Let me break this down by the key drivers of MRR growth, starting with our Net Revenue Retention, or NRR, which came in at 115% for the quarter. That's up from 112% in Q1 and well above our long-term target of 110%+, reflecting strong customer stickiness and expansion within our existing base of over 2,800 customers. Notably, our Dollar-Based Net Expansion Rate, or DBNER, expanded to 128%, fueled by upsells and cross-sells into higher-tier modules like our AI-Driven DevOps Intelligence platform, which we launched in late Q4 last year. Expansions accounted for 24% of total MRR growth this quarter, with multi-year commitments from key accounts—think Fortune 500 names in financial services and retail—adding over $2.8 million in incremental MRR. For context, our top 10 customers grew their spend by an average of 35% YoY, validating our strategy of embedding deeper into mission-critical workflows.

New logo acquisition also contributed meaningfully, driving 18% of YoY MRR growth with 152 net new customers added, bringing our total Annual Contract Value, or ACV, from new wins to an average of $185K—up 12% from last year. This was propelled by our freemium-to-enterprise funnel, where we've seen conversion rates improve to 28% from self-serve signups, thanks to targeted inbound from content syndication on platforms like Gartner and G2. Churn remains a bright spot at just 3.2% gross dollar churn—down 40 basis points sequentially and among the lowest in the DevOps SaaS space—bolstered by our 98% renewal rate on contracts over $100K ACV.

Regionally, the trends are equally encouraging. The Americas, which represent 62% of our MRR at $28.0 million, grew 30% YoY, driven by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure that accelerated our go-to-market in SMBs and mid-market verticals like e-commerce and healthcare. EMEA, at 24% of MRR or $10.8 million, posted 25% YoY growth despite softer enterprise spending in Germany and the UK; our localized data sovereignty features, compliant with GDPR and the EU AI Act, helped us close deals with 15 new logos there, including expansions with logistics firms navigating supply chain disruptions. APAC was the standout at 14% of MRR, or $6.4 million, surging 38% YoY on the back of our Tokyo data center launch and joint go-to-markets with partners—adding 42 net new customers in Japan, Australia, and Singapore, where demand for our predictive churn analytics is exploding amid regional digital transformation pushes.

Looking under the hood, several technical initiatives were pivotal. Our Q1 investment in the "ForgeAI" suite—integrating generative AI for real-time pipeline forecasting and account 360 insights, powered by models fine-tuned on our proprietary dataset of 500 million+ interactions—drove a 15% attach rate in new deals and unlocked $1.2 million in MRR from upsells alone. We've also enhanced our API ecosystem, with 40% of expansions tied to custom integrations via Zapier and native connectors to tools like Jenkins and GitLab, reducing time-to-value and boosting our Net Promoter Score to 68. Usage-based pricing pilots in our developer platform cohort showed 22% higher retention versus fixed-price seats, a trend we'll scale enterprise-wide in H2.

Strategically, these MRR trends position us for sustained acceleration. While the broader SaaS market saw median growth dip to 22% YoY per Bessemer Venture Partners' latest Cloud Index—impacted by conservatism and bundling pressures—our 28% outperformance stems from a focused vertical strategy, with 55% of MRR now from high-LTV sectors like fintech and manufacturing. We're guiding for Q3 MRR of $47.5 million to $48.0 million, implying 27-29% YoY growth, with NRR holding at 114%+. Risks remain around potential churn spikes if recessionary pressures intensify, but our 18-month cash runway and $120 million in RPO visibility give us ample flexibility to invest in AI R&D and sales capacity.

Now, turning to churn analysis, which remains a cornerstone of our customer retention strategy here at CloudForge, the leading AI-powered DevOps SaaS platform serving over 12,000 mid-market and enterprise customers globally. In Q2 FY24, we delivered strong retention metrics that underscore the stickiness of our platform amid a challenging macro environment. Our gross dollar churn was 4.2% annualized, down 180 basis points year-over-year from 6.0% in Q2 FY23, and well below our long-term target of under 5%. Logo churn held steady at 3.8%, reflecting our focus on revenue protection over sheer customer count. Net revenue retention (NRR) expanded to 118%, up from 112% a year ago, driven by 28% NRR expansion from upsells and cross-sells. For context, this outperforms the median SaaS NRR of around 105-110% as reported in recent Battery Ventures benchmarks, and puts us in elite company with peers like ServiceNow at 120%+.

Let me break down the primary drivers of churn, based on our rigorous cohort analysis and exit surveys from the 320 logos we lost in the quarter—about 60% from the mid-market segment (ARR under $100K) and 40% enterprise. First, macroeconomic headwinds accounted for roughly 35% of churn. Persistent inflation and dev team budget freezes have led to 15-20% cuts in engineering spend, mirroring what we've seen industry-wide; Gartner notes that 42% of SaaS spend is under review in 2024. Our SMB-heavy cohorts from 2021-2022, acquired during the post-pandemic dev boom, were hit hardest, with churn spiking to 7.5% in those vintages.

Second, competitive displacement represented 25% of churn. We're seeing intensified pressure from incumbents like GitLab and Harness in the enterprise tier, particularly on pipeline integration modules, where we've lost 12 deals to their bundled offerings. Niche players are nipping at our heels in the mid-market with aggressive freemium models—about 8% of our churn tied to their all-in-one CI/CD combos. We've also observed a 10% uptick in EMEA churn to 5.8% annualized, driven by localized competitors capitalizing on GDPR-ready compliance tools amid rising data sovereignty regs.

Third, product and adoption issues made up 20%—think low net promoter scores (NPS dipping to 48 from 52 YoY) tied to underutilization of our AI pipeline analytics features. Exit data shows 40% of churned customers were using less than 30% of modules post-onboarding, often due to integration friction with legacy tools like Jenkins and GitHub Actions. The remaining 20% stems from mergers & acquisitions (M&A) consolidation—DevOps M&A volumes are up 25% YoY—and renewals timed poorly against fiscal year-ends.

On a positive note, trends are encouraging. Newer cohorts from FY24 show sub-3% churn at the 6-month mark, thanks to our revamped onboarding. Multi-year contracts now comprise 65% of bookings, up from 50%, buffering against annual renewals. Regionally, North America churn is a pristine 3.5%, APAC at 4.9% reflecting currency volatility, and EMEA stabilizing at 5.8% post our Dublin data center launch.

Our mitigation strategies are multifaceted, blending proactive customer success, product innovation, and data-driven pricing. Customer Success 2.0 is our flagship initiative: we've scaled our CS team by 25% to a 1:80 ARR coverage ratio, implementing mandatory 30-day onboarding playbooks that boosted Day 30 adoption from 65% to 82%. Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) now include AI-powered usage dashboards, identifying at-risk accounts 45 days earlier—our predictive churn model, built on XGBoost ML algorithms analyzing 200+ signals like login frequency and module depth, flags 85% of churners with 92% precision.

Product-wise, we're accelerating our roadmap: Q3 sees the launch of 'CloudForge Unite,' seamless bi-directional integrations with Jenkins, Terraform, and Slack, addressing 70% of integration pain points from surveys. We've embedded generative AI for automated compliance audits, targeting EMEA retention, and rolled out value-based pricing tiers—shifting from flat ARR to usage-linked models that increased NRR by 6 points in pilots. Expansion motions are firing on all cylinders: land-and-expand tactics yielded $18M in Q2 upsells, with 40% of customers expanding to our security analytics or deployment marketplace add-ons.

Strategically, we're doubling down on verticalization—fintech churn is now under 3% post-custom compliance modules—and partnering regionally, like our co-sell agreement with Microsoft for Azure embeddings in APAC. Looking ahead, we expect gross churn to dip below 4% by FY25E as these initiatives mature, supporting our 25%+ ARR growth guidance. Retention is not just a metric; it's our economic moat in this consolidating DevOps SaaS landscape.

I'll now turn to our full-year fiscal 2024 revenue guidance, which reflects our strong momentum across the business, disciplined execution on our land-and-expand strategy, and the accelerating adoption of our AI-powered platform amid a resilient enterprise spending environment.

For the full fiscal year ending December 31, 2024, we are introducing revenue guidance of $2.42 billion to $2.48 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 24% to 27%. This compares to our prior guide of $2.35 billion to $2.42 billion issued last quarter, which we now expect to meaningfully exceed. To put this in context, this guidance implies Q3 revenue of approximately $620 million to $635 million and Q4 of $655 million to $675 million, with sequential acceleration driven by seasonal strength in new customer wins and expansion within our existing base.

Let me break this down by key drivers, starting with our core subscription revenue, which comprises 94% of total revenue and is projected to grow 25% to 28% year-over-year to $2.28 billion to $2.33 billion. This is underpinned by several SaaS-specific tailwinds:

Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) Growth: We ended Q2 with ARR of $2.31 billion, up 26% year-over-year, and we now expect full-year ending ARR of $2.55 billion to $2.62 billion, a 25% to 28% increase. This reflects our dollar-based net retention rate (NRR) stabilizing at 112% for the year—up from 110% in FY23—fueled by upsell and cross-sell opportunities in our AI Workflow Suite. For instance, 40% of our top 500 customers have now adopted our GenAI modules, driving average expansion of 15-20% per account.

Customer Metrics: We added 1,450 net new customers in Q2, bringing our total to 18,200, with a focus on Fortune 1000 logos. Large enterprise ACV deals (> $1M) grew 35% YoY, representing 28% of Q2 bookings, as we benefit from multi-year contracts—now averaging 3.2 years—providing visibility and reducing churn to a trailing 12-month rate of just 5.2%, below our historical 6-7% range.

Product and Technical Initiatives: Revenue from our next-gen offerings, including the CloudForge AI Platform launched in Q1, is tracking at $450 million for the full year, or 19% of total revenue, up from 12% last year. Key enablers include our proprietary fine-tuned LLMs integrated with AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, enabling no-code workflow automation that has reduced customer time-to-value by 40%. We're also seeing early wins from our PartnerSync marketplace, with integrations to tools like SAP and Oracle contributing 15% of new ARR.

Regionally, our guidance assumes balanced growth:

Americas (72% of revenue): Expected to grow 26% to 29%, driven by public sector deals and financial services expansion amid regulatory tailwinds.

EMEA (18% of revenue): 22% to 25% growth, with strength in DACH and UK markets from GDPR-compliant AI features; we've offset softer Southern Europe macros with 30% YoY increase in seat-based expansions.

APAC (10% of revenue): Accelerating to 28% to 32% growth, led by Japan and Australia, where we've doubled our direct sales force and secured hyperscaler partnerships with Azure.

On the macro front, while we've navigated a cautious IT spend environment—echoing the "selective buying" trends Gartner highlighted in their 2024 Magic Quadrant for Workflow Automation—we're resilient due to our 85% gross margin profile and focus on mission-critical use cases like procurement automation and compliance workflows. Non-GAAP operating margins are guided to 28% to 29%, supporting $850 million in adjusted free cash flow.

Strategically, this guidance embeds continued R&D investment at 22% of revenue, prioritizing AI security (e.g., our Zero-Trust AI Guardrails) and vertical solutions for healthcare and manufacturing, where we've seen 50%+ win rates against incumbents like UiPath and Pegasystems. We remain committed to our capital allocation framework: 50% to share repurchases (with $400 million authorized remaining), 30% to tuck-in M&A like our recent $150 million acquisition of a low-code AI startup, and the balance to organic growth.

In summary, this full-year guide positions CloudForge for another year of market-share gains in the $100 billion+ SaaS automation market, with AI as our durable differentiator. We're well above consensus estimates and confident in delivering durable, profitable growth.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $2.42 billion to $2.48 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs.

John Doe:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI Copilot on your overall growth?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks for the question, John. Absolutely, ForgeAI Copilot has been a game-changer for our growth trajectory. As an LLM-powered tool automating 40% of pipeline debugging tasks, it has supercharged our product-led growth engine. We've seen inbound leads surge 48% year-over-year, contributing to over 60% of our pipeline through integrations with GitHub and our content ecosystem. In new deals, it boasts a 15% attach rate, directly fueling expansions and helping us shorten enterprise sales cycles by 22% to 67 days. Early adopters are realizing 3x faster release cadences, which has driven dollar expansion to 132% in enterprise accounts. Overall, it's central to our NRR of 118% and positions us to outpace the market in AI-driven DevOps adoption.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Emily. International expansion is a top priority, building on our regional momentum. North America remains dominant at 65-72% of revenue and customers, but EMEA has accelerated to 22-24% share with 35% YoY customer growth, thanks to GDPR-compliant AI features and our Dublin data center. We've closed key telco and logistics wins there despite softer spending. APAC is our fastest grower at 13-14%, up 55% YoY in new logos, powered by Tokyo data center, Snowflake partnerships, and hyperscaler co-sells—adding significant ARR from Singapore, Japan, and Australia amid cloud-native demand. For H2, we're doubling direct sales in APAC, launching localized features for the EU AI Act, and expanding PartnerSync marketplace integrations. We expect APAC to hit 28-32% growth for FY24, with balanced scaling across regions to derisk macro volatility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Mike Chen:
Thanks, Raj. As I detailed earlier, churn is well-controlled at 4.2% gross dollar annualized, down significantly YoY, with NRR at 118%. Macro headwinds like budget cuts drive 35% of it, but we've mitigated via Customer Success 2.0—scaling teams, 30-day playbooks boosting adoption to 82%, and AI predictive models flagging risks early with 92% precision. Product launches like CloudForge Unite for seamless Jenkins/Terraform integrations address adoption gaps, while value-based pricing and vertical plays (e.g., fintech under 3%) drive expansions worth $18M in Q2. Multi-year deals at 65% of bookings and 98% renewals on large ACVs provide stability. We expect further improvement below 4% by FY25, fortifying our moat.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
